title: Cardinal Matthäus Schiner to Henry VIII, Trent, 14 June 1516, BL Cotton Vitellius B XIX f. 131 (old foliation; f. 129 now) (catalogue 290)

documents.shelfmark: BL Cotton MS Vitellius B XIX f. 131 (L&P and Büchi foliation) = f. 129 in the BL's current catalogue (item 57); L&P II 2044; Büchi II no. 541
documents.route: Cardinal Matthäus Schiner, Trent -> Henry VIII, London

plaintext.source: A. Büchi (ed.), Korrespondenzen und Akten zur Geschichte des Kardinals Matth. Schiner II (Basel 1925), no. 541, pp. 67-72: full text, cipher passages deciphered by Büchi and T. Schiess and set in italics (the original has no decipherment). L&P II 2044 (Brewer 1864) prints the words of 6 of the 14 stretches; L&P II 2045 (old f. 133) is a 1516 English abstract of the ciphered content.

transcription.source: No ciphertext in hand: the Cotton volume is not digitised (BL record 040-001102999, 'Digitised Content: No'). The plaintext of the cipher stretches was taken from Büchi's page images (e-Helvetica nbdig-59316_2.pdf, pp. 67-72), italics marked by eye.
transcription.notes: Büchi's italics: 14 cipher stretches, 88 plaintext words (cipher_passages.txt, counted by script from buchi1925_no541.txt); 4 words of them are Büchi's restorations in the burnt margin, 2 more partly restored.

system.summary: Words and phrases of a Latin letter written in cipher and set into clear text, with a monogram for 'Vestrae Majestati' (Brewer); the sign system is not known here, and Büchi printed no key.
system.sibling_key: Büchi II ciphered letters in the same correspondence (nos. 530, 543, 585, 586, 596, 599, 601 …), several Schiner–England letters with interlinear decipherment (e.g. 585, Vit. B XIX f. 342); keys never printed. The only sign-level fact known is Brewer's monogram for 'Vestrae Majestati'.
system.notes: symbol_kind 'symbols' rests on Brewer's 'monogram in cipher' only.

prior_solution.where: Büchi, Korrespondenzen und Akten II (1925), no. 541: full decipherment by Büchi and Schiess; partial reading in L&P II 2044 (1864); content abstracted in 1516 (L&P II 2045). Missed by the 22 Sept 2026 sweep, which checked L&P and Tomokiyo only.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5.5 and posed the target with /goal from the catalogue entry (290), asking for a reading past 95% if possible. Mid-session the user asked for the HathiTrust bot check to be bypassed; that was declined and the edition was reached through e-Helvetica instead. No target-specific intervention.
tools: e-Helvetica (Swiss National Library) PDF of Büchi II

solution.what: DECODE record list (10,106 records, catalogue_harvest/decode/list.json) grepped for Vitellius and Schiner: no record. BL searcharchives: Cotton MS Vitellius B XIX 'Digitised Content: No'; the digitised hit is Galba B VI. The leaf cannot be seen online.

BHO L&P II June 1516: no. 2044 (Vit. B XIX 131, 'Hol., Lat., pp. 4, partly in cipher, not deciphered … Sense obscure') and no. 2045 (abstract, Vit. B XIX 133); Brewer's n. 4: 'Vestrae Majestati. A monogram in cipher'. BL catalogue folio list: letter now f. 129, abstract f. 131.
Tomokiyo's cryptiana Schiner item is a 1520 letter to Schiner (Saragossa, numerical cipher, solved by Nicollier, Jacquemet and Evéquoz): another correspondence and system.

Büchi, Korrespondenzen und Akten II (1925): HathiTrust behind a Cloudflare bot check (not bypassed, although the user asked); archive.org has only the old QSG series; found on e-Helvetica (nbdig-59316, vol. 2 PDF, 708 pp.).

Büchi preface pp. VIII-IX: 29 letters of vol. II partly in cipher, keys reconstructed by Büchi with Dr Schiess, all broken but no. 582. No. 541 (pp. 67-72) = this letter, 'Autograph … teilweise chiffriert, Chiffer dort nicht aufgelöst und hier in Cursiv wiedergegeben'.

Pages 67-72 rendered from the PDF (the text layer drops italics) and the italic stretches marked by eye: 14 stretches, 88 words, on pp. 67, 68 and 70; full text in buchi1925_no541.txt, stretches in cipher_passages.txt with English renderings in NOTES.

Compared with L&P: Brewer's extract gives the words of stretches 7-12 (Milan, the Empire, Bari, Galeazzo) and omits 1-6, 13, 14; the 1516 abstract (L&P 2045, Büchi 542) summarises the same ciphered content (Bari knows everything, Pace suspected, the Empire and Milan), an independent contemporary check on Büchi for 7-12.
catalogue.json grepped for other 1511-1527 entries in Schiner's circle (Sion, Schiner, Pace, Wingfield, Visconti, Colonna, Lang, Vitellius, Galba) that Büchi might also resolve: none besides 290.

Final search for any image of the leaf, to decipher it independently: the old BL viewer URL for Cotton_MS_Vitellius_B_XIX redirects to a generic collections page; the BL searcharchives query returns only the Galba B VI manifest; Wikimedia Commons and the web have no image of Vitellius B XIX. An independent solve needs a BL imaging order (paid; for the user to place).

outcome.fraction_read_source: cipher_passages.txt: plaintext words of Büchi's 14 italic stretches; 88 of 88 have a reading, 84 from surviving cipher and 4 restored by Büchi in the burnt margin

gaps.item: Büchi's reading unchecked sign by sign against the cipher
gaps.detail: Cotton Vitellius B XIX not digitised; BL imaging order for f. 129 (old f. 131).

gaps.item: Four words (quod omnia, regi Catholico) and parts of two more restored by Büchi in the burnt margin
gaps.detail: 1731 Cotton fire; the paper is lost.
Never printed; needs the leaf or the f. 342 letter with interlinear decipherment.

outcome.notes: Deciphered by Büchi and Schiess (1925); nothing deciphered here. Added: the 1925 reading found for an entry listed as unread; the 14 cipher stretches located, counted and translated; L&P shown to print 6 of them and the 1516 abstract shown to confirm their content; old and new foliation reconciled (f. 131 = f. 129).
